newsitem.title: INDIA: Controversial Indian tax may be phased out - Chidambaram.
newsitem.headline: Controversial Indian tax may be phased out - Chidambaram.

text.p: Indian finance minister P. Chidambaram has said that a controversial corporate tax may be phased out after a new Income Tax Act and Companies Act came into force.

"The introduction of MAT (Minimum Alternate Tax) in the last budget has caused a high degree of discomfort to industry. It was introduced as a number of companies were paying dividend but not tax," he told a seminar organised by the International Association of Lawyers on Sunday, according to a report in the Financial Express.
Chidambaram's speech was also reported by other Indian newspapers on Monday.
Indian industry has complained that MAT ate into the profits of several companies this year, partly resulting in most half-year results of leading firms showing a fall in profits.

The Business Standard, reporting Chidambaram's speech, quoted him as saying that "with the company tax and the Income Tax Act being redrafted, it is possible to bring about a better alignment between the two and then there may be cause for MAT to disappear."
He said he would not like to comment further on this matter as parliament was in session.
